newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE to issue new one-month euromark future.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE to issue new one-month euromark future.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Monday it would issue a new one-month euromark interest rate futures contract on November 21, 1996.
The new contract was being launched as part of the exchange's strategy for European Economic and Monetary Union, (EMU), LIFFE said in a statement.

"The increased level of volatility between three-month and one-month deutschmark interest rates highlights the requirement for an additional hedging and trading tool -- a market need which will be met by the launch of this new contract," the LIFFE statement said.

LIFFE said its decision to launch the new futures contract was also based on increased activity in deutschmark LIBOR-based Forward Rate Agreements (FRAs) and interest rate swaps, increased issuance by the Bundesbank of short-term paper, and market and member demand.
LIFFE said details of the new contract would be as follows:
DELIVERY DAY First business day after the last
LAST TRADING DAY 11.00 two business days prior to
the third Wednesday of the delivery
"EMU is the greatest challenge facing European financial futures and options exchanges," Jack Wigglesworth, LIFFE's Chairman, said in the statement.
"Part of LIFFE's stated EMU strategy is to enhance our range of products, and, in particular, along the deutschmark yield curve."
LIFFE said the new contract would trade by open outcry on the LIFFE trading floor.
